timeline.draft_answer: The three most important pseudocereals are buckwheat, quinoa, and amaranth, all of which can be grown easily in Switzerland. Quinoa and amaranth originated in South America, while buckwheat comes from Asia and was historically widespread in Europe until 20th-century cereal breeding advances pushed it aside. Buckwheat still has potential to supplement major calorie crops, though its seed yield is around half that of the big cereals. At ETH Zurich, researchers at the World Food System Center (WFSC), with support from Coop, have examined buckwheat diversity, conducted taste tests, begun describing its genomic diversity, and identified the most suitable buckwheat varieties for Switzerland. The chunks focus on buckwheat research specifically and do not detail dedicated ETH research on quinoa or amaranth.
